case.messenger-archive-search.title: Messenger Archive & Semantic Search
case.messenger-archive-search.problem: Search text and transcribed audio by meaning in a private message archive.
case.messenger-archive-search.context: A personal project that separates message import, transcription and indexing so each step can be retried.
case.messenger-archive-search.architectu: Rust loads message records through MTProto. PostgreSQL stores records and transcription jobs. A Python worker runs Whisper, and a Rust indexer stores embeddings in Qdrant. An MCP interface exposes search.
case.messenger-archive-search.challenges: Parallel workers can encounter jobs that another worker already claims.
The vector store and the indexing checkpoint are separate systems.
Use PostgreSQL row-level locks with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED to let workers skip conflicting rows.
Map each vector upsert to a deterministic UUIDv5 ID.
Advance the index checkpoint after the vector write succeeds.
case.messenger-archive-search.reliabilit: A retry can repeat a vector write to the same point ID. Unrelated side effects need their own deduplication.
A crash between stages can leave work to replay. Progress is tracked at each completed stage.
case.messenger-archive-search.results.1: Combines message and transcript search in an MCP interface.
case.messenger-archive-search.provenance: Independent personal project. The diagram describes software components and contains no example messages or account records.
case.entity-concurrency-locking.title: EntityLocker — Row-Level Entity Concurrency Utility
case.entity-concurrency-locking.problem: Explore how Java threads can coordinate by an entity key within one process.
case.entity-concurrency-locking.context: EntityLocker is an independent Java utility with JUnit cases for several locking behaviours.
case.entity-concurrency-locking.architec: A concurrent map associates entity IDs with reentrant lock objects. A thread-local value records the current acquisition order and rejects a lower nested ID. Registry removal is attempted when a critical section exits.
case.entity-concurrency-locking.challeng: Nested key acquisition can create dependency cycles.
Retiring a key safely requires coordination with both current holders and contenders.
case.entity-concurrency-locking.decision: Use one ordered key type and reject decreasing acquisitions on the same thread.
Keep the lock registry inside each EntityLocker instance.
case.entity-concurrency-locking.reliabil: Tests cover same-key access, reentrancy, timeouts and rejection of decreasing lock order.
Registry retirement needs additional stress testing. Separate instances or processes do not share these locks.
Illustrates JVM-local keyed locking and why safe reclamation needs separate verification.
case.entity-concurrency-locking.provenan: Public source and JUnit tests for a Java locking experiment maintained by Denis Stepulenok.
case.rust-desktop-tooling.title: RustShot Desktop Capture
case.rust-desktop-tooling.problem: Capture screenshots across different desktop environments with a common command-line interface.
case.rust-desktop-tooling.context: RustShot is an independent Rust utility for Windows, Linux and macOS.
case.rust-desktop-tooling.architecture: Platform-specific adapters acquire an image and send it to the requested output destination. Linux Wayland can use the desktop portal. Windows also supports screen recording.
case.rust-desktop-tooling.challenges.1: Operating systems expose different capture capabilities.
case.rust-desktop-tooling.challenges.2: Desktop portal workflows depend on the caller’s desktop session and permissions.
case.rust-desktop-tooling.decisions.1: Document platform support separately for screenshots, region selection and recording.
case.rust-desktop-tooling.decisions.2: Keep capture and output handling separate.
case.rust-desktop-tooling.reliability.1: Repository tests cover capture helpers and output behaviour. Live desktop checks depend on the platform.
case.rust-desktop-tooling.results.1: Provides screenshot capture on three desktop platforms and documents their feature differences.
case.rust-desktop-tooling.provenance.sum: Public RustShot capture guide and source maintained by Denis Stepulenok.

diagram.messenger-archive-search.label: Personal archive with message import, row-level job claiming, transcription, vector indexing and MCP search.
diagram.messenger-archive-search.title: Semantic Search & MCP Integration
diagram.messenger-archive-search.summary: A personal archive with separate import, transcription and vector indexing stages. Retries can replay an upsert to the same point ID.
diagram.messenger-archive-search.provena: Independent personal project. The diagram describes software components and contains no example messages or account records.
diagram.messenger-archive-search.node.mt: Provides incremental message history and voice attachments subject to upstream rate limits.
Rate-limited upstream API requires persistent cursor checkpoints to avoid costly full re-syncs.
diagram.messenger-archive-search.node.ru: Fetches history with exponential/flood-wait backoff and stores raw messages in PostgreSQL.
Rust async runtime handles long-running sync sessions with predictable memory footprint.
diagram.messenger-archive-search.node.po: Claim available rows using row-level locks
Workers claim transcription jobs in PostgreSQL with row-level locks. SKIP LOCKED lets a worker select other eligible rows while locks are held.
Available rows can be claimed out of arrival order when earlier jobs are locked.
diagram.messenger-archive-search.node.wh: A Python worker runs Whisper on claimed audio and stores the transcript for indexing.
Jobs need retry or recovery rules for work that stops before completion.
diagram.messenger-archive-search.node.ru: The indexer assigns a deterministic vector ID and advances its checkpoint after the upsert succeeds.
Writes can be replayed after a crash. The vector store and checkpoint do not share an atomic transaction.
diagram.messenger-archive-search.node.qd: Stores semantic embeddings keyed by deterministic UUIDv5 identifiers derived from message identity.
Deterministic IDs avoid duplicate entries when the same vector is written again after a restart.
diagram.messenger-archive-search.node.mc: Exposes semantic search and thread retrieval tools to LLM assistants over Model Context Protocol.
Read-only query tools isolate LLM agents from direct database or session credentials.
diagram.entity-concurrency-locking.label: JVM-local keyed locking with a lock registry, lock acquisition, action execution and attempted registry retirement.
diagram.entity-concurrency-locking.title: JVM-Local Entity Locking
diagram.entity-concurrency-locking.summa: EntityLocker explores keyed locking among Java threads in one process. The code orders nested acquisition and attempts to retire idle registry entries.
diagram.entity-concurrency-locking.prove: Public source and JUnit tests for a Java locking experiment maintained by Denis Stepulenok.
Concurrent Caller Threads
Threads in one JVM pass an entity key
Threads using the same EntityLocker instance supply the key and code they wish to run.
Distributed coordination
The lock registry is local to one instance. Other instances and processes are outside its scope.
Concurrent Lock Registry
Look up a lock object by ID
ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent associates a present key with a lock object.
Cache consistency
Idempotency
Safe retirement also requires coordination with the lock holders and contenders.
Per-ID Reentrant Lock
Reentrant lock with an optional timeout
The utility checks nested ID order within the calling thread, then uses a reentrant lock for blocking or timed acquisition.
Failure handling
Distributed coordination
The ordering check applies to nested calls through the utility. Other locks can still participate in dependency cycles.
Protected Critical Section
Run the action and release the lock
When acquisition succeeds, the utility runs the caller’s action and releases the lock in a finally block.
Cache consistency
Rollback, where needed, relies on the resources or application code used by the action.
Registry Retirement
Attempt to remove unused registry entries
The implementation tries to retire an entry before releasing its current lock.
Observability
Failure handling

diagram.ref-event-driven-outbox.label: Educational outbox flow from a local database transaction through publication, delivery and duplicate handling.
diagram.ref-event-driven-outbox.title: Transactional Outbox & Idempotent Event Consumer
diagram.ref-event-driven-outbox.summary: An educational reference for committing an event with application data and relaying it to a broker. Repeated publication is possible, so consumers need a duplicate-handling strategy.
diagram.ref-event-driven-outbox.provenan: Independent reference design for teaching a general engineering pattern.
diagram.ref-event-driven-outbox.node.app: Write business data and an outbox entry
Use one local database transaction to update business data and persist the intended event.
Atomicity covers this database transaction. The later broker publication is a separate operation.
diagram.ref-event-driven-outbox.node.db-: Persist an event in the local transaction
Make each committed event available to a relay, with a stable identifier.
The outbox retains a pending event when the relay is unavailable. Broker delivery follows separate configuration.
diagram.ref-event-driven-outbox.node.out: Publish pending events to the broker
Read pending rows, publish to the broker and record progress after acknowledgement.
A crash after publication but before recording progress can make the relay publish again.
diagram.ref-event-driven-outbox.node.bro: Buffer and deliver events according to the broker configuration.
At-least-once delivery can repeat messages. Delivery settings and failure behaviour vary by broker.
diagram.ref-event-driven-outbox.node.ide: Handle repeats with an event ID
Deduplicate effects within a defined boundary, for example by writing a processed event ID and a local state change in one transaction.
Other effects need their own mechanism. A database deduplication record does not protect an unrelated external call.
diagram.ref-event-driven-outbox.node.dlq: Retain failed messages for inspection after the configured retry policy is exhausted.
Replaying a failed message still requires a duplicate-handling strategy.
diagram.ref-async-job-pipeline.label: Educational asynchronous job flow from submission and claim through bounded execution, output publication and monitoring.
diagram.ref-async-job-pipeline.title: Resilient Asynchronous Job Queue & Backpressure
diagram.ref-async-job-pipeline.summary: An educational reference for accepting jobs, constraining worker concurrency and publishing completed outputs.
diagram.ref-async-job-pipeline.provenanc: Independent reference design for teaching a general engineering pattern.
diagram.ref-async-job-pipeline.node.api-: Authenticates requests, enqueues work asynchronously, and returns a job correlation ID immediately.
Keeps request threads fast and predictable instead of blocking on long-running background work.
diagram.ref-async-job-pipeline.node.job-: Persist queued work and record a worker’s claim before execution.
Retries and expired claims may allow a job to run again. Make effects safe to repeat.
diagram.ref-async-job-pipeline.node.boun: Use a bounded worker pool to apply backpressure and keep job execution within configured limits.
Higher concurrency increases resource use. Backpressure moves waiting time into the queue.
diagram.ref-async-job-pipeline.node.atom: Write a temporary output and publish it with a replacement operation where the storage system supports it.
Atomic replacement is storage-dependent. A queue acknowledgement is a separate operation.
diagram.ref-async-job-pipeline.node.metr: Monitor queue depth, job age and failure counts to identify delays or repeated errors.
Signals need thresholds and investigation. Durability depends on storage and retry behaviour.
concept.1.name: Idempotency
concept.1.description: Repeating an operation has the same effect within a defined boundary. A stable key can prevent duplicate records without covering unrelated effects.
concept.2.name: Eventual Consistency
concept.2.description: Separate stores may disagree while updates are in progress. Retries and reconciliation can help them converge when the changes are applied.
concept.3.name: Message Delivery Guarantees
concept.3.description: At-least-once delivery can repeat a message. Exactly-once processing requires a clearly defined transaction and effect boundary.
concept.4.name: Failure Handling
concept.4.description: Recover from transient faults through bounded retries, and expose persistent failures for inspection or replay.
concept.5.name: Distributed Coordination
concept.5.description: Threads in one JVM can share a lock. Multiple processes need a coordination mechanism with its own failure model.
concept.6.name: Cache Consistency
concept.6.description: Cached data can become stale. Expiry, invalidation and refresh policies determine when it becomes consistent with its source.
concept.7.name: Observability
concept.7.description: Logs, metrics and traces help explain behaviour and investigate failures.
concept.8.name: Security
concept.8.description: Use authentication, authorisation, appropriate data handling and a documented threat model to protect access.
